name: No Child Left Behind
title: No Child Left Behind is signed
text: The 2001 reauthorization of federal education law required every state to test reading and math in grades 3 to 8 and once in high school, publish results by subgroup, and show "adequate yearly progress" toward every student reaching proficiency by 2014, with sanctions for schools that missed. It was the high-water mark of federal test-based accountability.

name: Common Core
title: The Common Core standards are released
text: Shared reading and math standards written by a state-led effort and released in June 2010. Forty-five states adopted them within two years, helped by the $4.35 billion Race to the Top competition in the 2009 stimulus, which rewarded states that took on common standards and teacher evaluation tied to test scores. Several states later repealed or renamed them.

name: ESSA
title: The Every Student Succeeds Act is signed
text: The replacement for No Child Left Behind kept annual testing but handed the design of accountability back to the states and ended the federal "adequate yearly progress" targets. It is the law still in force.

name: COVID closures
title: Schools close for COVID-19
text: By the third week of March 2020 nearly every public school in the country had closed its buildings. Most reopened in some form during 2020-21, many remote or hybrid for the full year. The 2022 NAEP results, the first after the closures, showed the largest drops in the assessment's history.

name: ARP relief
title: The American Rescue Plan sends $122 billion to schools
text: The third and largest round of federal pandemic relief for K-12, on top of $67 billion in the two earlier rounds. Districts had until early 2025 to spend it. It is the largest one-time federal investment in schools on record.
